lines.text: It’s capstone time! Today you will build a complete website for a cause or idea you care about.
Choose something real that matters to you, like a park clean-up or a book swap.
Ask who the page is for and what you want visitors to do.
Your answer becomes the goal of your whole page.
Give each section an id, like id equals gallery.
A link with href set to hash gallery jumps straight to that section.
A row of these links at the top is called a nav bar.
Your gallery uses flexbox cards from lesson five.
Your form uses the labels you learned in lesson six.
Your button uses the JavaScript you learned in lesson seven.
Check every picture has alt text and a credit, and every label is joined.
Click every button and link in the live preview.
Make sure there are no personal details and that every claim is honest.
The hash in the link means a place on this same page.
It jumps to the section whose id matches the word after the hash.
The header tag holds the title and tagline at the top of the page.
The footer holds the credit line at the bottom, using a club name, not your full name.
A small button makes the page feel alive.
It uses the same find, listen and change pattern from last lesson.
Before launch day, go down this checklist one line at a time.
Fix anything that is not ticked, then press Check and submit with your reflection.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now plan it, build it, test it, and share it!
